questions.text: If for a square matrix A, A² − 3A + I = O and A⁻¹ = xA + yI, then the value of x + y is :
questions.solution: Multiply A² − 3A + I = O by A⁻¹: A − 3I + A⁻¹ = O, so A⁻¹ = −A + 3I. x = −1, y = 3, x + y = 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The range of the function f(x) = 2 sin⁻¹x + 3π/2, where x ∈ [−1, 1], is [π/2, 5π/2].
Reason (R): The range of the principal value branch of sin⁻¹(x) is [0, π].
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: 2 sin⁻¹x ∈ [−π, π], so f(x) ∈ [π/2, 5π/2]: A is true. The principal range of sin⁻¹ is [−π/2, π/2], so R is false.

Assertion (A): The equation of a line passing through the points (1, 2, 3) and (3, −1, 3) is (x − 3)/2 = (y + 1)/3 = (z − 3)/0.
Reason (R): The equation of a line passing through points (x₁, y₁, z₁) and (x₂, y₂, z₂) is given by (x − x₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = (y − y₁)/(y₂ − y₁) = (z − z₁)/(z₂ − z₁).
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: The direction ratios are (2, −3, 0), so the line is (x − 3)/2 = (y + 1)/(−3) = (z − 3)/0. A is false; R is the standard two-point form, true.

questions.text: A function f : A → B defined as f(x) = 2x is both one-one and onto. If A = {1, 2, 3, 4}, then find the set B.
questions.solution: Since f is onto, B is exactly the set of images: B = {2, 4, 6, 8}.

questions.text: Show that the function f(x) = 16 sin x/(4 + cos x) − x is strictly decreasing in (π/2, π).
questions.solution: f′(x) = [16cos x(4 + cos x) + 16 sin²x]/(4 + cos x)² − 1 = (64cos x + 16 − (4 + cos x)²)/(4 + cos x)² = cos x(56 − cos x)/(4 + cos x)². In (π/2, π), cos x < 0 and 56 − cos x > 0, so f′(x) < 0: f is strictly decreasing.

questions.text: Evaluate : ∫ from 0 to π/2 of [log(sin x) − log(2 cos x)] dx.
questions.solution: ∫₀^(π/2) log sin x dx = ∫₀^(π/2) log cos x dx (using x → π/2 − x). So the integral is −∫₀^(π/2) log 2 dx = −(π/2) log 2.

questions.text: Find the particular solution of the differential equation dy/dx + sec²x · y = tan x · sec²x, given that y(0) = 0.
questions.solution: IF = e^(tan x). y e^(tan x) = ∫ tan x sec²x e^(tan x) dx = (tan x − 1)e^(tan x) + C, so y = tan x − 1 + Ce^(−tan x). y(0) = 0 gives C = 1: y = tan x − 1 + e^(−tan x).

questions.text: Solve the differential equation x dy − y dx − √(x² + y²) dx = 0.
questions.solution: dy/dx = (y + √(x² + y²))/x is homogeneous. Put y = vx (x > 0): x dv/dx = √(1 + v²), so log|v + √(1 + v²)| = log|x| + log C. Hence y + √(x² + y²) = Cx².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A and B are independent events such that P(A ∩ B̄) = 1/4 and P(Ā ∩ B) = 1/6. Find P(A) and P(B).
questions.solution: Let P(A) = a, P(B) = b: a(1 − b) = 1/4 and b(1 − a) = 1/6. Subtracting, a − b = 1/12. Substituting, 12b² − 11b + 2 = 0, so b = 2/3 or 1/4. Hence P(A) = 3/4, P(B) = 2/3, or P(A) = 1/3, P(B) = 1/4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A relation R is defined on the set of real numbers R as R = {(x, y) : x · y is an irrational number}. Check whether R is reflexive, symmetric and transitive or not.
questions.solution: Not reflexive: 1 · 1 = 1 is rational, so (1, 1) ∉ R. Symmetric: xy = yx. Not transitive: (1, √2) ∈ R and (√2, 2) ∈ R, but 1 · 2 = 2 is rational, so (1, 2) ∉ R.

questions.solution: Direction AB ∝ (2, 3, 6). Line: r = (i + 2j − 4k) + λ(2i + 3j + 6k); (x − 1)/2 = (y − 2)/3 = (z + 4)/6. Distance between the parallel lines = |(a₂ − a₁) × b|/|b| with a₂ − a₁ = (2, 1, −1): (2, 1, −1) × (2, 3, 6) = 9i − 14j + 4k, magnitude √293. Distance = √293/7 units.

questions.text: Find the area of the region bounded by the curves x² = y, y = x + 2 and the x-axis, using integration.
questions.solution: The line meets the x-axis at (−2, 0) and the parabola at x = −1 (and x = 2). The region enclosed by all three lies between x = −2 and x = 0: area = ∫₋₂⁻¹ (x + 2) dx + ∫₋₁⁰ x² dx = 1/2 + 1/3 = 5/6 square units.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
A tank formed using a combination of a cylinder and a cone offers better drainage as compared to a flat bottomed tank. A tap is connected to such a tank whose conical part is full of water. Water is dripping out from a tap at the bottom at the uniform rate of 2 cm³/s. The semi-vertical angle of the conical tank is 45°.

Find the volume of water in the tank in terms of its radius r.
questions.solution: With semi-vertical angle 45°, h = r, so V = (1/3)πr²h = πr³/3.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
A tank formed using a combination of a cylinder and a cone offers better drainage as compared to a flat bottomed tank. A tap is connected to such a tank whose conical part is full of water. Water is dripping out from a tap at the bottom at the uniform rate of 2 cm³/s. The semi-vertical angle of the conical tank is 45°.

Find the rate of change of radius at an instant when r = 2√2 cm.
questions.solution: dV/dt = πr² dr/dt = −2. At r = 2√2: dr/dt = −2/(8π) = −1/(4π) cm/s.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
A tank formed using a combination of a cylinder and a cone offers better drainage as compared to a flat bottomed tank. A tap is connected to such a tank whose conical part is full of water. Water is dripping out from a tap at the bottom at the uniform rate of 2 cm³/s. The semi-vertical angle of the conical tank is 45°.

Find the rate at which the wet surface of the conical tank is decreasing at an instant when the radius r = 2√2 cm.
questions.solution: Slant height l = √2 r, so the wet surface S = πrl = √2πr². dS/dt = 2√2πr dr/dt = 2√2π(2√2)(−1/(4π)) = −2. It decreases at 2 cm²/s.

Find the rate of change of height h at an instant when the slant height is 4 cm.
questions.solution: l = √2 h = 4 gives h = r = 2√2. Since h = r, dh/dt = dr/dt = −1/(4π) cm/s.
